correctness.rationale: For squarefree m supported on primes q congruent to 2 mod 3, sigma(m^2)=product_{q|m}(q^2+q+1). If a support prime p divides q^2+q+1 with p not equal q, then q has order 3 modulo p; this is impossible for odd p congruent to 2 mod 3 because 3 does not divide p-1, while p=2 cannot divide the odd factor. The diagonal factor q^2+q+1 is 1 modulo q. Hence gcd(m,sigma(m^2))=1, so both GCDs in Dris’s defining equality equal 1. The Dirichlet series F(s)=product_{p congruent 2 mod 3}(1+p^{-s}) satisfies F(s)^2=(zeta(s)/L(s,chi_3))(1-3^{-s}) product_{p congruent 2 mod3}(1-p^{-2s}); Selberg–Delange therefore gives B(x)~C x/sqrt(log x), and using L(1,chi_3)=pi/(3 sqrt3) yields C=(1/pi)sqrt(2 sqrt3 product_{p congruent2 mod3}(1-p^{-2}))=0.498208218... . Fixed-omega subfamilies follow from choosing exactly r such primes.
risks: The asymptotic uses the standard Selberg–Delange theorem for a prime set of Dirichlet density 1/2; it says nothing about the full density of Dris’s set.

originality.rationale: Dris’s full Section 5 was inspected. It observes that primes and prime powers are solutions, proves only that the full set has density below one, and conjectures density zero; it also quotes a different obstruction driven by primes p congruent to 1 mod 6. It does not identify the squarefree support on primes 2 mod 3, prove gcd=1 there, or count that family. Fresh Resultary searches found nearby sigma/divisor-sum records but none implying this support theorem or its x/sqrt(log x) asymptotic.
residual_risks: A classical multiplicative-number-theory note could contain the same prime-support observation without using Dris’s set notation; targeted searches did not surface one.

value.rationale: The family is structurally motivated by the cyclotomic factor q^2+q+1 in the very GCD problem Dris studies. It yields an explicit infinite subfamily of all support sizes and a sharp first-order count of order x/sqrt(log x), giving quantitative lower structure inside a set conjectured to have density zero.
risks: It is a lower-bound family, not an asymptotic for the full GCD set.

limitations: Only the squarefree subfamily supported on primes congruent to 2 modulo 3 is classified.
No conclusion on the full asymptotic density of Dris’s set.
